en.headline: Police record 2,020 messaging hijack cases in seven months
en.dek: Instant-messaging account takeovers rose 154 per cent from January to July, police said, with WhatsApp involved in 99 per cent of cases.
body: Police said they recorded 2,020 instant-messaging account hijacking cases in the first seven months of 2026, a 154 per cent increase from 795 cases in the same period last year. Combined losses were about HK$150 million, down 22.7 per cent from a year earlier.

WhatsApp accounted for 1,993 of the cases, or 99 per cent, up 169.7 per cent from 739 a year earlier, with losses of about HK$146 million. Other platforms included Telegram and Facebook in small numbers. Police said overall technology crime still fell 13.9 per cent to 16,437 cases in the same period, with losses of about HK$3.08 billion.

Cyber Security and Technology Crime Bureau Superintendent Rachel Hui Yee-wai said most takeovers began with phishing messages that impersonated WhatsApp’s official service centre and warned of an imminent account suspension. After victims entered a phone number and verification code on a fake site, she said, scammers studied chat histories, then impersonated relatives or colleagues. About 1,591 cases, or 80 per cent, involved someone posing as a family member or friend.

Police cited cases in which an investment-company finance manager transferred HK$12.2 million after instructions arrived from a supervisor’s hijacked account, and a businessman lost more than HK$10 million after a deepfake voice message imitated his father. Another victim paying a property deposit lost about HK$1.17 million after scammers used new numbers and the real names and profile pictures of an estate agent and a solicitor. Officers advised the public not to click unsolicited links and to confirm any transfer request through a separate channel before sending money.

zh.headline: 首7個月通訊軟件騎劫案升154% 99%涉WhatsApp
zh.dek: 警方錄得2,020宗即時通訊帳戶騎劫案，按年升一倍半，損失約1.5億元，當中絕大部分發生在WhatsApp。
body: 警方表示，今年首7個月錄得2,020宗即時通訊軟件帳戶騎劫騙案，較去年同期795宗上升154%。損失金額約1.5億元，按年減少22.7%。
當中1,993宗、即99%涉及WhatsApp，較去年同期739宗上升169.7%，損失約1.46億元。其餘個案散見Telegram及Facebook等平台。警方指，同期整體科技罪案有16,437宗，按年跌13.9%，損失約30.8億元。
網絡安全及科技罪案調查科警司許綺惠表示，大部分騎劫由釣魚短訊開始，騙徒假扮WhatsApp官方服務中心，以帳戶即將停用作招來，誘使事主在假網站輸入電話號碼及驗證碼。得手後，騙徒會翻查對話紀錄，再模仿語氣向親友或同事借錢。約1,591宗、即八成案件，是假冒家人或朋友。
警方舉例，有投資公司財務經理按被騎劫的上司帳戶指示，轉帳1,220萬元；另有商人收到疑以深偽技術生成、假扮父親的語音訊息，損失超過1,000萬元。亦有事主買樓期間，被騙徒用新號碼套用經紀及律師頭像，騙去約117萬元訂金。警方呼籲市民勿隨意點擊來歷不明連結，遇轉帳要求應另開渠道核實對方身分，並核對收款帳戶名稱。
